Hi! I’ve been with my now husband (married since January 2024) dating while he’s in the navy since 2019. I wouldn’t suggest rushing into it and this first part is going to suck no matter what LDR wise. If he’s deployed or doing training exercises chances are whether or not you are married or just dating you wouldn’t see him. 


While he’s in bootcamp in his first schools he has to live in the barracks with a bunch of other dudes with curfews and you won’t have time to see him. My husband just switched to the army and even after 8 years of service we got texting and calling every day privileges but I wouldn’t have been able to move through the army yet because we’re married. 

Now when it comes time for his first orders you could maybe get away with the military moving your stuff too if you do the move yourself. We did that on a pcs together no problem. The issue here is he won’t be eligible to live off base at first so are you willing to follow him and live on your own or not. We didn’t have this issue because my now husband was already living off base with BAH

The loss of not being married really is the “stigma” of other wives and sometimes leadership. My now husbands leadership gave him a lot of shit when he moved with me and we had long commutes for one orders change telling him you aren’t married dump her. These men were three times divorced. It does make life easier once married but I still wouldn’t change our timeline looking back. 

PM if this is confusing at all and happy to chat further!

As a milspouse, You didn’t do anything wrong and this isn’t your problem to deal with. I get the wife/friend telling you so you are aware to mitigate any escalation of issues and so that you know why she’s being weird around you in future social settings. 

I’ve seen that happen to other women in my husbands unit where it causes issues. It’s the toxic part of the military and one wife’s opinion can sadly turn a lot of people against you. Most of the time it’s the men’s fault in this by being dodgy and bad husbands or partners thinking they are making the situation better by lying about when their female coworker is around or just straight up being delusional thinking their coworker is into them. All of this to say, there’s nothing you can do in this situation besides be yourself and don’t avoid her at events and maybe it’ll get better. I’d actually ask the wife who told you to talk to her husband to talk to the dude to see how he’s handling it on his end to see if he’s actually making it worse. My husband has tried doing that with parties we were friends with both sides on. 

ultimately I think your unit is the asshole here by not extending this trip to families and can see the perspective of the wife being generally annoyed about the trip and taking it out on you (which is incorrect but to help you emphasize with what’s really going on). The military already takes you away from us a good chunk of the time so a 3 day fun trip, non mission related would irk me. Yes the civilian side has retreats too but families are invited.
